articles.title: Mamdani’s Oct. 7 commemoration outrages supporters and critics of Israel
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani tried to thread a needle on the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attacks by condemning Hamas’ “horrific war crimes” and denouncing Israel’s “genocide” in Gaza. It did not go well.

articles.title: 3 injured following 2 separate house explosions in Hamilton, occurring around 90 minutes apart
articles.summary: Three people are in hospital — two with serious injuries — following two separate house explosions in different areas of Hamilton on Thursday morning. articles.title: Oshawa museum faces nearly $3K in city fines over homeless encampments on property
articles.summary: A charity that runs a museum in Oshawa has received nearly $3,000 in city fines for allowing "nuisance activity" on its property. It says it needs help, not penalties, to keep the museum safe from vandalism, trespassing and damage.

articles.title: Man dead after industrial accident in Brampton, police say
articles.summary: A man is dead after an industrial accident in Brampton on Wednesday, Peel police say.

articles.title: How transit expansion is driving the Scarborough North municipal election
articles.summary: Toronto city council races are heating up, and Ward 23 Scarborough North is a key one to watch. With major transit infrastructure being built and plans for subways extending further into the area, the ward is undergoing massive change. CBC’s Dale Manucdoc breaks down the race and who is running to represent the community.

articles.title: New documentary about Ridgeway Plaza tackles its negative reputation
articles.summary: 'Meet Me At Ridgeway,' a new film by Mississauga residents, explores the controversial plaza's cultural richness, challenges, opportunities for voter engagement and takeaways for urban planners and the City of Mississauga.

articles.title: Kenneth Law case: Families reveal the devastating toll in 'The Poison Seller'
articles.summary: Mississauga’s Kenneth Law pleaded guilty to aiding suicide after selling lethal chemicals online to people around the world. A CBC investigation linked Law to at least 147 deaths, but the real number might never be known. articles.title: What needs to change in Toronto? We asked residents
articles.summary: We asked downtown Toronto residents what the biggest issues are in their neighbourhood. Their answers? Homelessness, affordability and transit reliability. This is the latest instalment of Toronto Speaks, where CBC’s Alejandrina Alvarez visits neighbourhoods across the city to hear what matters most to your community.

articles.title: Police search for driver, witnesses after fatal hit and run in Vaughan
articles.summary: York police responded to a report of an unresponsive person found on the side of the road in Vaughan on Tuesday at 2 p.m. The woman, 60, was a live-in caregiver on her way to work when she was struck by a vehicle that fled the scene.

articles.title: Family overjoyed after beloved pet bunny Biscuit, who was stolen from Markham fair, safely returned
articles.summary: The family of Biscuit, the fluffy Holland Lop rabbit who was stolen from the Markham Fair over the weekend, says he has been found and safely returned home.

articles.title: Toronto police investigate suspected hate-motivated arson after reports of Israeli flags lit on fire
articles.summary: Toronto police are investigating a suspected hate-motived arson after it was reported several Israeli flags were lit on fire in North York early Wednesday.

articles.title: Retail theft increasingly 'sophisticated' and now work of organized crime, experts say
articles.summary: Retail theft has evolved from individual shoplifting into a crime increasingly committed by organized criminal networks, according to Peel Regional Police.
